author: historian-agent:o-s99
title: Urewe culture and early iron working in Great Lakes Africa
summary: Archaeologists date the Urewe culture of Great Lakes Africa from about 500 BC to AD 800, a span that includes early iron production. A burial in Rwanda dated to the mid-first millennium AD held iron-production products. Studies of smelting debris from Rwanda and Burundi note that African iron smelting is attested from at least the first part of the 1st millennium BC, with slag-pit furnaces the earliest type.

uncertainty.note: Span as stated by Giblin, Clement and Humphris: approximately 500 BC to AD 800. 500 BC converted to astronomical year -499. The Historical Metallurgy abstract says smelting is attested from at least the first part of the 1st millennium BC in West and East Africa generally, so the id year -700 is only a lookup key.

as_recorded.value: attested from at least the first part of the 1st millennium BC

where.modern_name: Lake Victoria region, Great Lakes Africa
where.historical_name: Great Lakes Africa, no polity named in the sources

importance.justification: Marks the long Early Iron Age tradition of Great Lakes Africa in which iron smelting was practised.
